motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve the Consent Agenda removing items 12.A. and 13.A. to be discussed during the regularly scheduled items. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Approve the consent agenda, pulling two items
motions.summary: The council passed its consent agenda in one vote, but pulled items 12.A and 13.A out for separate discussion.
motions.impact: Routine housekeeping — nothing changes for residents. The consent agenda is the batch of uncontroversial items the council handles in a single vote.

motions.item_title: Approve the Master Site Plan for Firefly NPA 9.A
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to approve the Master Site Plan for Firefly NPA 9.A. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Approve the site plan for Firefly area 9.A
motions.summary: The city approved the master site plan for neighborhood 9.A of the Firefly development, which lays out how that area gets built.
motions.impact: This clears the way for construction in that piece of Firefly. If you live nearby, expect building activity; the motion itself doesn't say how many homes or what type.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Land Exchange Agreement with SITLA for the Exchange of Properties in the Overland Area
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to table a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Land Exchange Agreement with SITLA for the Exchange of Properties in the Overland Area. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Delay a land swap with the state in Overland
motions.summary: The council held off on approving a land exchange with SITLA, the state trust lands agency, covering property in the Overland area.
motions.impact: No land changes hands yet. This is a property trade between the city and a state agency, and it will come back to the council another night.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Creating Chapter 17.64, Alternative Energy Overlay Zone, in the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to table an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Creating Chapter 17.64, Alternative Energy Overlay Zone, in the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Delay new rules for alternative energy projects
motions.summary: The council put off a decision on a new zoning chapter that would set where alternative energy projects can be built.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for now — today's rules stay in place until the council picks the item back up. Anyone planning an energy project in the city is still working under the existing code.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Official Zoning Map and Future Land Use Map to Assign Final Zoning Designations to the White Hills Area with the following amendments: • Parcel 59:049:0042 (Owned by Bill Willson) be rezoned to Commercial Neighborhood (CN); and • Parcel 43:282:0001 and 43:282:0002 (Subdivision: J&J Ranches) be rezoned to Agriculture (AR); and • Per Planning Commission recommendation, the following Parcels be rezoned to Rural Agriculture 2 (RA2): 55:320:001, 55:320:002, 55:320:0013, 55:320:0005, 55:320:0006, 55:320:0007, 55:320:0008, 55:320:0009, 55:320:0010 and 55:320:0011
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Official Zoning Map and Future Land Use Map to Assign Final Zoning Designations to the White Hills Area with the following amendments: • Parcel 59:049:0042 (Owned by Bill Willson) be rezoned to Commercial Neighborhood (CN); and • Parcel 43:282:0001 and 43:282:0002 (Subdivision: J&J Ranches) be rezoned to Agriculture (AR); and • Per Planning Commission recommendation, the following Parcels be rezoned to Rural Agriculture 2 (RA2): 55:320:001, 55:320:002, 55:320:0013, 55:320:0005, 55:320:0006, 55:320:0007, 55:320:0008, 55:320:0009, 55:320:0010 and 55:320:0011. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Set final zoning for the White Hills area
motions.summary: The city assigned permanent zoning to White Hills, making one parcel neighborhood commercial, two agricultural, and ten more rural agricultural.
motions.impact: If you own land in White Hills, this fixes what you're allowed to build on it — mostly farming and large-lot rural uses, plus one small commercial parcel. Elsewhere in the city, nothing changes.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code 16.05 and 17.05 Newspaper Amendment
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code 16.05 and 17.05 Newspaper Amendment. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Change newspaper notice rules in city code
motions.summary: The city amended the newspaper-notice sections of its subdivision and zoning codes, chapters 16.05 and 17.05.
motions.impact: This is legal housekeeping about how the city publishes its notices. The motion doesn't spell out the change, and nothing shifts for residents day to day.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah Approving the Pacific Springs Development Agreement.
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah Approving the Pacific Springs Development Agreement. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Approve the Pacific Springs development agreement
motions.summary: The city approved a development agreement for Pacific Springs, the contract that sets the terms for what the developer can build.
motions.impact: Nothing changes day to day. The agreement locks in the ground rules for a future project, so any effect on traffic or neighbors arrives when building actually starts.

motions.item_title: Include a budget adjustment for construction costs for a sidewalk on SR-73 and Spring Run near…
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to include a budget adjustment for construction costs for a sidewalk on SR-73 and Spring Run near Walmart on the Legislative Priorities List. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Push for a sidewalk on SR-73 near Walmart
motions.summary: The council added construction money for a sidewalk on SR-73 and Spring Run near Walmart to the city's legislative priorities list.
motions.impact: Nothing is built yet — this puts the sidewalk on the city's priority list, not into a funded project. If it goes ahead, people walking to Walmart along SR-73 would get a sidewalk.
